evidence.paraphrase: The page provides frequently updated model estimates of current-quarter headline and core CPI and PCE inflation before all official observations are released.
The system combines daily oil prices, weekly gasoline prices, and monthly CPI and PCE releases in a compact mixed-frequency information set.
Monthly inflation projections are combined into quarter-over-quarter annualized nowcasts for the corresponding official price indexes.
Disrupted or missing official months require explicit handling, and nowcast quality must be assessed against statistical and survey benchmarks rather than inferred from fit alone.

executive_summary: The Cleveland Fed inflation-nowcasting page describes a small, deliberately structured mixed-frequency system for current-quarter CPI and PCE inflation. Daily oil, weekly gasoline, and monthly official price releases update headline and core measures, with monthly forecasts aggregated to quarterly rates. The useful product lesson is release-aware component updating and benchmarked real-time error, not the claim that a few market prices explain all inflation mechanisms.

method_routes.sample_definition: real-time daily, weekly, and monthly information available before each CPI/PCE release

questions.question_text: How can high-frequency energy prices and partial monthly releases update current-quarter U.S. CPI and PCE inflation before the official quarter is complete?
